subject: Results in mirt and in IRTPRO 3 program

messages.author: e8d938cf9ec973b4
messages.subject: Results in mirt and in IRTPRO 3 program
parts:
Can someone explain why I obtain different a, b, and c parameters estimates when I use IRTPRO3 and the package mirt from R?

The method both uses are Bock and Aiken (1981) - IRTPRO calls BAEM and R calls EM.

I have estimated the parameters with default options both in IRTPRO and with mirt package, but the results are quite different.

My sample consists of 96 items with 180 respondents.

In IRTPRO the configurations (from mysets.irtpro) are

    Estimation:
        Method = BAEM;
        E-Step = 500, 1e-005;
        SE = S-EM;
        M-Step = 50, 1e-006;
        Quadrature = 49, 6;
        SEM = 0.001;
        SS = 1e-005;
    Scoring:
        Mean = 0;
        SD = 1;
    Priors:
        (Q_1, Slope[0]) = Lognormal, 0, 1;
        (Q_1, Guessing[0]) = Beta, 4, 16;
        (Q_2, Slope[0]) = Lognormal, 0, 1;
        (Q_2, Guessing[0]) = Beta, 4, 16;
        (Q_3, Slope[0]) = Lognormal, 0, 1;
        (Q_3, Guessing[0]) = Beta, 4, 16;
        (Q_4, Slope[0]) = Lognormal, 0, 1;
        (Q_4, Guessing[0]) = Beta, 4, 16;
        (Q_5, Slope[0]) = Lognormal, 0, 1;
        (Q_5, Guessing[0]) = Beta, 4, 16;
    .
    .
    .

And in R I ran

    mirt(test_result, 1, itemtype='3PL')

The first 10 results for estimated parameter in **R** are

               a        b     g u
    Q_1    0.413   -3.454 0.062 1
    Q_2    0.807   -0.115 0.262 1
    Q_3   -0.460    3.967 0.249 1
    Q_4    3.827   -1.121 0.962 1
    Q_5    2.896    0.090 0.636 1
    Q_6    0.328   -1.556 0.030 1
    Q_7    0.931    2.879 0.003 1
    Q_8   -5.402   -2.415 0.058 1
    Q_9    2.810   -0.406 0.810 1
    Q_10   0.003  -18.079 0.161 1

The first 10 results in **IRTPRO** are

               a                       b                     g
    Q_1        0.39                    -2.92                    0.2
    Q_2        0.77                    -0.12                    0.19
    Q_3        0.13                    -14.18                    0.2
    Q_4        0.8                        -5.77                    0.2
    Q_5        0.69                    -1.7                    0.2
    Q_6        0.31                    -0.36                    0.19
    Q_7        0.37                    109220.43                0.09
    Q_8        0.37                    26016.14                0.08
    Q_9        0.95                    -2.75                    0.2
    Q_10    0.12                    0.43                    0.21

I see that there are priors in IRTPRO estimates ( (Q_1, Slope[0]) = Lognormal, 0, 1; (Q_1, Guessing[0]) = Beta, 4, 16; ). Is that the case to set this priors in mirt? If so, what is that configurations. I tried to use parprior option, but without success.

I'm very new to IRT analysis. But I need to get the same results in IRTPRO and in mirt to validate de estimates in IRTPRO.

Can someone help me?

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Results in mirt and in IRTPRO 3 program
parts:
Check the example files in ?mirt first, within the first example there's a 3PL model run with prior. Also see ?mirt.model for learning how the syntax works. 

You may want to search through this forum as well to get a better understanding of why mirt doesn't support beta priors for the g and u parameters. I might at some point, but it will require some tweaking which I'm not terribly interested in getting around to. Cheers.

Phil
